findings.title: Settlement issue treats Node `split-required` as a terminal failure, with no recovery on reopen
findings.evidence: examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2939 — `issueSettlement` maps every `!issued.ok` result to a throw. A displaced source with multiple intents is re-issued as one multi-operation `issueLocal`, which Node routes through the application-batch path and can answer `localIssueSplit(prefixLength)` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6662-6665). Replacements are assigned fresh, numerically larger logical times (index.ts:2996-2997), so a source that originally fit the budget can exceed it once re-batched, and a `transform` that grows operations can do the same. The legacy path handles this by splitting and retrying (index.ts:2651-2664); the settlement path instead rejects `drainSettlementOutbox`, which sets `terminalFailure` (:3217-3219) and fails every public `issue()` (:4074-4076). The condition is deterministic, so every reopen reproduces it and the room is permanently unopenable. Fail-closed — no double-apply and no safety violation — but there is no recovery path.
findings.required_action: Handle `split-required` in `issueSettlement` (split the replacement operations and retry the prefix/suffix as the legacy path does), or record an explicit disposition stating that a settlement replacement may never exceed the application batch budget and why.

findings.title: Plan-recorded f5b0c P2 ownership is reassigned and partly dropped in the slice's own evidence
findings.evidence: docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:99249 and :99267-99269 assign f5b0c four P2s: room typecheck, replacement `planEffect` authority, authenticated frontier threading with classifier-local terminal suppression, and same-store activation-digest runtime coverage. Room typecheck is discharged (result.json `typecheck: pass`) and replacement `planEffect` authority is exercised (index.ts:2936). But .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0c-green-3b6a66a9/deferred.md reassigns authenticated frontier threading to f5b and is silent on same-store activation-digest runtime coverage, and no commit amends the plan record. The frontier deferral is structurally forced — `readSettlementSources` passes `settlementFrontier: undefined` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:8642-8647) and no settlement checkpoint exists until f5b — so the substance is defensible; the record is not, and the plan doc still names f5b0c as owner. The plan doc also has no D.110c-0c1f5b0c entry at all, unlike the closed sibling slices.
findings.required_action: At slice close, amend the plan record to state the f5b0c GREEN, move frontier threading/terminal suppression to f5b with the dependency reason, and give same-store activation-digest runtime coverage an explicit owner rather than letting it lapse.

findings.title: Settlement path is gated on a second, pre-verification derivation of the profile with its own decode limits
findings.evidence: examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1572-1581 decodes `material.exactCanonicalProfileBytes` with local limits `{maxBytes: 65_536, maxDepth: 4, maxItems: 128}` and gates the whole settlement drain (:3035, :3046, :3209) on the result. The authoritative value is the verified `openedTrust.trust.profileId` (:4214-4221), which is also what Node gates on (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6246, :8092); the control-plane decodes its trust carrier with default limits (packages/control-plane/src/creator-trust-checkpoint-advance.ts:120-121). Divergence is infeasible today because the genesis anchor binds `profileDigest` over exactly these bytes (:773) and any mismatch fails closed at the Node fence check, so this is not a live defect. It is two owners for one fact: the room-local `decodeCanonical` is unguarded, so a carrier the trust path accepts but that exceeds `maxItems: 128` throws out of session creation instead of opening.
findings.required_action: Thread the verified `openedTrust.trust.profileId` into the drain gate instead of re-deriving it from invite bytes, or state the decode-limit parity requirement explicitly and hand it to the W1 decode-limit-parity owner.
